name: The Undercroft Stair
summary: Four sandstone steps to a dais where the great tun lies on its cradles, casks along the north wall, and the butler's table with its lantern and tally sticks.
description: At the foot of the cellar stair the butler keeps his best wine where he can watch it: the great tun, a cask too big to carry through any door in the castle, lies on a raised dais at the top of four steps, a spigot in its head and a pewter jug waiting beside it. Two lesser casks rest along the north wall, and two upright barrels in the far corner hold whatever the kitchen has asked for. The butler's table in the south-east has a lantern, a pair of jugs and a bundle of notched tally sticks recording every measure drawn, which do not add up.
build: Shell: the kit's Crypt shell, 12.0 × 12.0 × 0.30 m slab, 0.50 m dressed-sandstone walls 3.00 m clear, a 0.45 m dark trim course, an archway 2.60 × 2.16 m centred on every wall.

Stair and dais (NW): the kit's stair-to-dais in sandstone: four steps 2.20 m wide, 0.35 m tread, 0.25 m rise, north along the west wall from y 1.90 to 3.30, then the dais 2.20 × 2.20 × 1.00 m in the corner (x −5.50 … −3.30, y 3.30 … 5.50).
The great tun: a cask r 0.55 m, 1.40 m long, lying north–south on two oak cradle blocks at (−4.60, 4.40) on the dais, two iron hoops, an iron spigot in its south head.
Jug: a pewter jug 0.28 m on the dais at (−3.70, 4.90).
NE casks: two casks r 0.40 m, 1.00 m, lying east–west on cradles against the north wall at x 2.80 and 4.40, y 5.00.
Butler's table (SE): oak 1.20 × 0.70 m, top 0.80 m at (3.60, −3.60): a steel lantern with a lit madder window, two pewter jugs, three tally sticks; an oak stool r 0.18 m at (3.60, −2.95).
Barrels (SW): two upright oak barrels r 0.40 m, 0.90 m, two hoops each, at (−4.80, −4.80) and (−3.90, −4.90).
The crossing: bare floor between all four archways.
sockets: Archway ×4, centred on each wall: 2.60 × 2.16 m (Crypt), all open
Dais: 1.00 m above the floor, reached by the stair; the jug on it is a loot anchor
Butler's table: a loot anchor at 1.10 m

materials.name: Oak
materials.notes: Casks, cradles, table, stool, tally sticks.

gameplay: The dais is a raised lookout over the crossing; the tun on it is full cover.
The stair's foot faces open floor, so the dais can be reached from the crossing.
Two loot anchors: dais and table.
